newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Tutu appeal as S.African amnesty deadline nears.
newsitem.headline: Tutu appeal as S.African amnesty deadline nears.

text.p: Nobel peace laureate Desmond Tutu on Sunday made an impassioned plea to South Africans across the politcal spectrum who were involved in apartheid-era crimes to request amnesty within the next six days.

Tutu, speaking on a television programme dedicated to the work of his Truth and Reconciliation Commission, emphasised the deadline for amnesty was on May 10 and that anyone who had not come forward to confess was liable for criminal prosecution.
"This is a cry from the heart," Tutu said. "I appeal to all of you, right across the political spectrum, please take this golden opportunity to apply for amnesty on the most generous terms possible."

The truth commission, whose role is to heal the wounds of the past by exposing the human rights abuses committed by both sides of the apartheid divide, has so far received some 5,500 applications for amnesty.

Many of the requests have been from former members of the government's security forces. Up to 300 members of the African National Congress have also applied, including Defence Minister Joe Modise, for the party's armed struggle against apartheid.
The two surviving apartheid-era presidents, P.W. Botha and F.W. de Klerk, have not applied.
